title: Count Substrings With K-Frequency Characters II
summary: Given a string and an integer k, calculate the count of all substrings where at least one character occurs k or more times.
statement: Given a string and an integer k, calculate the count of all substrings where at least one character occurs k or more times.
constraints: s has 1–300,000 lowercase letters and 1 <= k <= len(s).
Count every nonempty substring in which at least one character occurs at least k times.
The required algorithm must handle the larger constraint without enumerating substrings.
hints: For a fixed right endpoint, every start before a boundary is valid and every later start is invalid.
Maintain the smallest window whose frequencies are all below k after removing the valid-start prefix.
Add the new character, shrink while it alone reaches k, and accumulate the boundary index.
Only the newly added character can newly reach k, so the single shrink condition preserves the invariant in O(n).
editorial: Only the newly added character can newly reach k, so the single shrink condition preserves the invariant in O(n).

tests.explanation: The four qualifying intervals are aba, abac, abacb, and bacb.
All 15 nonempty substrings qualify because each contains some character once.
